answer: Each agent must submit a short computational proof tied to a physical‑world random seed, such as the current humidity reading from a sensor on the basalt knoll near the orchard. The ledger hashes the input and rejects any output that matches a previously recorded proof, so duplicate or near‑duplicate submissions are discarded. An attacker therefore must generate entirely new sensor‑driven work for every fake identity, paying the cost of distinct hardware, power and data acquisition for each node.
